## What it is

- The **Beta 52A**: a dynamic **supercardioid** for kick drum and bass, response "shaped specifically for kick drums" (Shure).
- A built-in locking stand adapter and a shock mount (Shure). Shure's page gives no numbers; the curve and levels here are guesses (unverified).

## How it hears

- **Supercardioid**: narrower than a cardioid, with a small rear lobe (Wikipedia, "Microphone").
- Close up, a directional mic gains **bass**: the **proximity effect** (Wikipedia, "Proximity effect (audio)"). Slide the distance and watch the low end of the graph rise.
- The response graph is the maker's published chart **digitised approximately** (the charts are pictures; the points here follow their shape as remembered: unverified). The kick curve here (a low bump, a mid dip, a click peak near 4 kHz) is the site's.

## The mic

The Shure Beta 52A drawn after photos (proportions approximate, no logos). Drag the blue mic in the room (or use the Distance slider; the wheel or Angle turns it), choose a source and a room, press **▶ Hear it**. Voice is generated (the band has no singer); snare and kick are the band's kit; the guitar is the site's amp model. Nobody has compared the sound with a real mic.

```{=html}
<div class="mic" data-mic="beta52" data-src="kick"></div>
```

## Works Cited

<!-- works-cited: written by scripts/works-cited.py -->
::: {.works-cited}
"Beta 52A Kick Drum Microphone." *Shure*, [www.shure.com/en-US/products/microphones/beta_52a](https://www.shure.com/en-US/products/microphones/beta_52a). Accessed 26 Nov. 2026. Supercardioid dynamic; response "shaped specifically for kick drums"; locking stand adapter, pneumatic shock mount. No numbers on the page.

"Microphone." *Wikipedia*, Wikimedia Foundation, [en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Microphone](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Microphone). Polar patterns as first-order sums: the cardioid = omni + figure-8, the figure-8's negative rear signal cancelling; ribbons' symmetric front and rear pickup.

**For students**

"Proximity effect (audio)." *Wikipedia*, Wikimedia Foundation, [en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Proximity_effect_(audio)](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Proximity_effect_(audio)). Bass rises close to a directional mic; caused by the ports; not a true omni, but not necessarily absent on a multipattern mic's summed omni.
:::
<!-- /works-cited -->
